theme.showcase.meta.title: CFPress — a WordPress-style CMS on the Cloudflare edge
theme.showcase.meta.desc: A WordPress-style CMS running entirely on Cloudflare Workers / D1 / R2 / KV: multi-site, multilingual, plugin and theme systems — and it never runs third-party code.
theme.showcase.hero.kicker: On the Cloudflare edge · never runs third-party code
theme.showcase.hero.sub: Themes, plugins, multi-site, multilingual content, members, a media library and a block editor — inside a single Cloudflare Worker. No server to maintain, and none of the extension model that makes WordPress installs a standing security target. Extensions are data, not code.

theme.showcase.hero.figcap: Real capture from a local wrangler dev run — 24 migrations, bilingual demo content, three sites on one Worker
theme.showcase.hl.title: Four decisions that go against the grain
theme.showcase.hl.sub: Each answers a real long-term cost in the WordPress world — security debt, language plugins, network config, server bills.
theme.showcase.f1.title: Third-party code never runs
theme.showcase.f1.p1: WordPress lets any plugin run arbitrary PHP in your request path — the root cause of its security record. CFPress makes the opposite choice: a theme is declarative templates rendered by a restricted engine; a plugin is a manifest declaring capabilities. Uploaded ZIPs are stored, never executed.
theme.showcase.f1.p2: The trade-off is stated plainly: declarative theming is less expressive than arbitrary PHP. That is the deal, on purpose.
theme.showcase.f1.imgalt: A theme declaring custom post types, routes, fields and blocks
theme.showcase.f2.title: Multi-site and multilingual, built in
theme.showcase.f2.p1: In WordPress, multilingual needs a plugin and multi-site needs a network config. Here both are first-class at the storage layer: every table carries an ownership declaration, every query is scoped by site_id, and deleting a site leaves no registry residue. Each locale version gets its own slug, URL and feed entry — not a translated copy in a plugin side table. A missing translation 404s rather than silently serving another language.
theme.showcase.f3.title: One post, two languages
theme.showcase.f3.p1: The switcher at the top of the editor is the post's language versions. The languages a site serves, a piece of content is written in, the admin interface uses, and a theme's business data is translated into — four independent layers. A Chinese admin behind an English site is a normal configuration, not a workaround.
theme.showcase.f3.imgalt: Block editor with the language-version switcher
theme.showcase.f4.title: Three sites, one Worker
theme.showcase.f4.p1: Routing matches by path prefix first (longest wins), then by host. Content, settings, menus, media and the active theme are all stored per site. The whole CMS — front-end rendering plus 16 admin modules — lives in one Worker, with no build step in the repository.
theme.showcase.box.title: A complete CMS with no server
theme.showcase.box.sub: Workers, D1, R2 and KV all have free allowances. CFPress is built to run inside them: a free-plan deploy is a working CMS, not a broken one.
theme.showcase.box.content.p: Posts and pages, categories, tags, block editor, revisions, autosave, scheduled publishing on a 5-minute cron
theme.showcase.box.media.p: R2-backed library, a shared picker, ownership scoping per site
theme.showcase.box.multisite.p: Storage-level isolation, per-site settings, per-site user roles
theme.showcase.box.languages.p: Content and UI languages, per-locale slugs, hreflang, per-locale feeds and sitemaps
theme.showcase.box.members.p: Front-end registration and accounts, separate from admin identity
theme.showcase.box.access.p: admin / editor / author capability matrix, enforced server-side
theme.showcase.box.themes.p: Declarative engine, packaged as ZIP, stored in R2, ships 3 examples
theme.showcase.box.plugins.p: Manifest-declared capabilities, settings schema, notification channels
theme.showcase.box.caching.p: Search API over published content; cache versioning invalidated automatically on content change
theme.showcase.cmp.title: A comparison of shapes, not a benchmark
theme.showcase.cmp.note: Not a like-for-like benchmark — a comparison of shapes. CFPress is the right choice when you want a CMS with no server and a smaller attack surface. It is the wrong choice when you need the WordPress plugin ecosystem, because that ecosystem is precisely what it refuses to run.
theme.showcase.qs.title: Four commands, up and running
theme.showcase.qs.desc: Create the two account-scoped resources, write their ids into a gitignored config file, start the dev server — on port 47913 (avoiding the SQLITE_BUSY caused by fighting other Wrangler projects over 8787). Change the default password on first login: credentials published in a public repository are not secrets.
theme.showcase.lic.title: AGPL-3.0, or a commercial license
theme.showcase.lic.agpl.p: For running your own site, internal systems, evaluation, study, and any project that is itself AGPL-3.0. Running it unmodified as your own site carries no obligation beyond keeping the notices intact.
theme.showcase.lic.comm.p: Required when you offer CFPress to third parties as a hosted service without releasing your modifications, or embed it in a closed-source product. The AGPL adds one obligation over the GPL: run a modified version as a network service, and you must offer the corresponding source to that service's users.
theme.showcase.cta.title: Take “maintain a server” off the build list
theme.showcase.cta.sub: The demo restores its content hourly — front end and admin are both open for a walk-through. Demo credentials are for the demo only.
